sentences.text: THIS CRIMINAL PETITION HAVING BEEN HEARD AND RESERVED ON 11.04.2023.

COMING ON FOR PRONOUNCEMENT OF ORDER THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER

This Criminal Petition is filed by the petitioner seeking to quash the proceedings in Crime No.48/2022 for the offences under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506 read with Section 149 of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.

2. Brief facts of the case are as under:
It is the case of the prosecution that the complainant married Rahul Gada on 29.04.2016.
At the time of the marriage, it is stated that dowry was given in the form of cash, gold, silver and also household articles.
It is stated in the complaint that she was taken care only for 15 days.
Thereafter, the petitioners used to demand to bring additional dowry and also abusing her in filthy language and causing harassment mentally.
In the meantime, she was taken to Bengaluru and staying with her husband.
In the meantime, the complainant became pregnant and delivered a female child.
It is stated that the petitioner was insulting the complainant as she gave birth to a female child.
The petitioner used to harass the complainant both mentally and physically.
It is further stated in the complaint that the complainant meted out the cruelty at the hands of the petitioner, which provoked her to commit suicide.

Thus being the fact, on 10.02.2020 at about 8-00 a.m., when the complainant was in Bengaluru, the petitioner being husband started quarreling with her and demanding a car to be purchased and given to him as dowry, when she refused to yield his demand, she was thrown out of the house along with the child.
Consequently, it is constrained to stay with her parents' house at Bidar.
It is stated in the complaint that the alleged demand of dowry and harassment given by the petitioner from 13.05.2016 to 10.02.2020.
Hence, a complaint came to be lodged on 31.07.2022.
The police have registered the case in Crime No.48/2022 for the above said offences.

sentences.text:
Heard Sri Aditya Sondhi, learned senior counsel appearing on behalf of Sri Basavaraj M. Police Patil and Sri Ajay Jawali, learned counsel for the petitioner, Sri Gururaj V. Hasilkar, learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent No.1 and Sri Jairaj K. Bukka, learned counsel for respondent No.2.
4.
It is the submission of the learned counsel for the petitioner that the respondent No.2 made out certain allegations against the petitioner, who is her husband.
The allegations are trivial matrimonial issues.
All the quarrels in the matrimonial home cannot be construed as harassment and cruelty.
To attract the ingredients of provisions under Section 498A of IPC, there must be harassment given to the wife, which drive her to commit suicide.
It is further submitted that respondent No.2 even though married in the year 2016, four years she lived with the petitioner happily and she gave birth to a female child.
The respondent No.2 even for petty reason used to quarrel with the petitioner and harassing the petitioner mentally and did not allow him to work in good atmosphere.
5. It is further submitted that the allegations made against the petitioner are not sufficient to face the trial.
Even assuming that the petitioner faces the trial, it would not be sufficient to convict him by means of such allegations.
Hence, subjecting him to face the trial certainly would affect his carrier and he is working in reputed company and having high stake in the society.
Making such submissions, the learned senior counsel prays to allow the petition.

6. Per contra, the learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent No.1/State vehemently opposed the petition stating that respondent No.2 specifically made out a case against the petitioner and overt-act against the petitioner is very clear from the averments of the complaint.
It is not appropriate to quash the proceedings without conducting the detailed trial as there are triable issues made out against the petitioner.

7. The learned counsel for respondent No.2 vehemently opposed the petition submitting that the petitioner is the husband of respondent No.2 and there are specific allegations made out against him regarding cruelty, harassment and demand of dowry.
A detailed trial is required to be held to unearth the truth.
It is further submitted that the Courts usually not to interfere in the matter where prima facie allegations are made out against the petitioner.
As such, he prays to dismiss the petition.

8. After having heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and also perused the averments made in the complaint, now it is necessary to refer the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Neeharika Infrastructure Private Limited vs. State of Maharashtra and others1.

sentences.text: Therefore, when the investigation by the police is in progress, the court should not go into the merits of the allegations in the FIR.
Police must be permitted to complete the investigation.
It would be premature to pronounce the conclusion based on hazy facts that the complaint/FIR does not deserve to be investigated or that it amounts to abuse of process of law.

xiii) The power under Section 482 Cr.P.C. is very wide, but conferment of wide power requires the court to be cautious.
It casts an onerous and more diligent duty on the court;

xiv) However, at the same time, the court, if it thinks fit, regard being had to the parameters of quashing and the self- restraint imposed by law, more particularly the parameters laid down by this Court in the cases of R.P. Kapur (supra) and Bhajan Lal (supra), has the jurisdiction to quash the FIR/complaint; and xv) When a prayer for quashing the FIR is made by the alleged accused, the court when it exercises the power under Section 482 Cr.P.C., only has to consider whether or not the allegations in the FIR disclose the commission of a cognizable offence and is not required to consider on merits whether the allegations make out a cognizable offence or not and the court has to permit the investigating agency/police to investigate the allegations in the FIR."
9.

Thus, on careful reading of the dictum of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, it discloses that when a prayer for quashing FIR or charge sheet is made by the accused/petitioner, the Court when it exercises the power under Section 482 of Cr.P.C., only has to consider whether or not the allegations in the FIR disclose the commission of cognizable offence and it is not required to consider on merits.
10. Regard being had to the dictum of the Hon'ble Supreme Court and also the averments of the complaint, the complainant made out prima facie allegations against the petitioner.
Whether the demand of dowry made by the petitioner and whether has he assaulted the respondent No.2 on 10.02.2020 is a matter of fact and a detailed trial is required.
Hence, I am of the considered opinion that the petition deserves to be dismissed.

11. In the light of the observations made above, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Criminal Petition is dismissed.

In view of disposal of the main matter,
I.A.No.1/2022 filed for stay does not survive for consideration and the same is disposed of.
